newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: REITH WELCOMES LATEST WAGE FIGURES
Federal Small Business and Workplace Relations Minister Peter Reith has welcomed the latest wage figures.
The Bureau of Statistics figures show lower than expected wages growth.
Average weekly earnings rose by only 0.5 per cent in the three months to May.
The figures show full-time adult wages have risen by a modest 3.7 per cent over the past year, well below general market expectations.
Speaking in Cairns, Peter Reith said the figures are a "plus" for business, but he refused to say whether interest rates should be cut.
Mr Reith said while monetary policy is the responsibility of the Reserve Bank, he does welcome the latest figures.
"The latest wage numbers are basically a confidence booster for the business community, they're down on the previous quarter, they're going in the right direction", he said.
POLICE HAVE MOST SUCCESS IN MURDER INVESTIGATIONS-SURVEY
New figures suggest police have most success in murder and attempted murder investigations.
The Bureau of Statistics has released a survey on the number of victims of crime in Australia last year.
The number of victims recorded rose for all offences in the poll, except for murder and motor vehicle theft.
Armed robbery and assault were among the highest increases. The study also examined the outcome of police investigations.
In more than 70 per cent of murder cases studied, police proceeded against offenders within 90 days, while the figure was more than 80 per cent for attempted murder.
Police were able to start proceedings in only about half of assault cases and about a third of armed robberies.
NEW SURVEY ON UNIVERSITY COURSES & SERVICES
The Federal Government has announced new measures aimed at improving the quality of teaching in universities.
The Government will conduct a new national survey of university quality, and $1.5 million will go into new awards for teaching excellence.
Education Minister Amanda Vanstone said the survey will gauge the standard of university courses and services, and tell students whether they are getting what they deserve.
She said both initiatives highlight the need for universities to put students first.
"Everything else that a university stands for and achieves depends on the health of its undergraduate teaching", she said.
NZ BUREAUCRAT BACKS CONCERNS ABOUT DEFENCE FORCE
A senior New Zealand bureaucrat has backed concerns in leaked Australian papers that New Zealand's defence force is no longer considered credible.
He is the deputy secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Neil Walter.
Mr Walter told a parliamentary select committee in Wellington that Australia's concern mirrors that of New Zealand's other key defence partners.
His comments follow a submission that a professional, credible and balanced armed forces is vital to New Zealand's place in the world.
When asked if New Zealand's armed forces met that criteria, Mr Walter said they fell short.
He called them balanced and professional, but not credible. - - - -
N.Z. MINISTER DESCRIBES AUSSIE BUREAUCRATS AS "MONGRELS"
A New Zealand Cabinet Minister has described as "Noddy bureaucrats" and "a pack of mongrels, the authors of the leaked Australian Foreign Affairs papers.
The Minister for Maori Affairs, Tau Henare, is demanding an apology from John Howard.
Mr Henare says the latest leaking of a Australian Government briefing paper, which described New Zealand spending on defence as inadequate, is the last straw.

He says a public apology should be immediately forthcoming from Australian, given that the Party's leader, Winston Peters, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, will be arriving in Melbourne tomorrow along with New Zealand's Prime Minister, Jim Bolger.
Mr Peters was described in an earlier leak as "a loose cannon and an opportunist".
Mr Henare says bureaucrats have no right to "slag off" other countries politicians.
He says he does not care if his choice of words is unwise because the briefing paper has greatly upset all New Zealanders. - - - -
WALLABY CAPTAIN CONFIDENT OF A WIN ON SATURDAY AT MCG
Australian Rugby Union captain John Eales says he is confident of an upset against New Zealand on Saturday night at the MCG.
The Wallabies trained for 90 minutes at Olympic Park this morning.
Eales says his team needs to lift in certain areas, and has put a lot of effort, this week, into scrum practice.
"Mentally I know the guys are very very keen to come up against New Zealand again and there's no one that's intimidated by playing them," he said.
Meanwhile it has been confirmed fullback Matt Burke will take over the goal-kicking duties from John Eales.
